title: Geometric and Weil fundamental representations
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, with $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, as in [def-tw-frobenius-action]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, assume $X$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and choose a geometric point $\bar x\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. A lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal F_0=(\mathcal F,\varphi)$ here means a lisse $\Qlb$-sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ in the convention of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], with an isomorphism
$$\varphi:\Phi_X^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F.$$
Here $\Phi_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, with $\gamma:z\mapsto z^{1/q}$, is geometric Galois Frobenius [def-tw-frobenius-action], and its pullback in precisely this lisse adic category is [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback]. No integral lattice stable under $\varphi$ is required.

Put $V=\mathcal F_{\bar x}$. The *geometric fundamental representation*
$$
\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}:\pi_1(X,\bar x)\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)
$$
is the stalk action of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2): at finite coefficients it is evaluation of the natural automorphism of the fibre functor [def-galois-fibre-functor], and it passes through inverse limits, rationalization and coefficient extension as in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Its continuity at a finite coefficient-field stage is in the sense of [def-pod-l-adic-representations].

Write $P=\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ and $G=\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)$. The maps in [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path], applied to the perfect field $k_0$, identify $P$ with the kernel of $r:G\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$. Define
$$
W(X_0,\bar x):=G\times_{\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)}\mathbf Z,
\qquad n\longmapsto\gamma^n.
$$
Thus it is the inverse image of the infinite cyclic subgroup generated by geometric Frobenius, with topology induced from $G\times\mathbf Z$, where $\mathbf Z$ is discrete. Its geometric subgroup $P\times\{0\}$ is open and has its profinite topology. Choose $s\in G$ with $r(s)=\gamma$, whose existence is supplied by [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path], and also denote $(s,1)\in W$ by $s$.

Use the canonical path
$$
\lambda_s:F_{\Phi_X\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar x}
$$
of [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path], specified on a finite cover descended to a finite extension of $k_0$ by the action of $s^{-1}$ on its arithmetic fibre. This specifies the path for the chosen lift, rather than only an isomorphism class of paths. Extend this finite path to lisse adic fibres using [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport], and use the pullback-fibre identification of [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback]. It gives a linear isomorphism
$$
L_s=\lambda_{s,\mathcal F}:(\Phi_X^*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}
       =\mathcal F_{\Phi_X\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}V.
$$
Define the degree-one operator by the specified composite
$$
T_s:=\varphi_{\bar x}\circ L_s^{-1}:V\xrightarrow{\sim}V.
$$
For clarity the conjugation convention is forced by these maps: if $\rho_\Phi$ denotes the $P$-action on $(\Phi_X^*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}$, the finite-path identity of [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path] and its adic extension in [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport] give
$$
 L_s\rho_\Phi(g)=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(s^{-1}gs)L_s.
$$
The stalk functor of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] takes $\varphi$ to an intertwiner, so $\varphi_{\bar x}\rho_\Phi(g)=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(g)\varphi_{\bar x}$. Substituting $g=shs^{-1}$ into the preceding identity gives
$$
T_s\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(h)
=\varphi_{\bar x}\rho_\Phi(shs^{-1})L_s^{-1}
=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(shs^{-1})T_s.
$$
Consequently $T_s\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(h)T_s^{-1}=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(shs^{-1})$ for $h\in P$.

Every $w=(u,n)\in W$ is uniquely $(us^{-n})s^n$ with $us^{-n}\in P$. The *Weil fundamental representation* of $\mathcal F_0$ is the extension defined by
$$
\rho(hs^n):=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(h)T_s^n
\qquad(h\in P,\ n\in\mathbf Z).
$$
This formula defines a continuous representation. Its construction is independent of the degree-one lift: [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path] gives $L_{as}=L_s\rho_\Phi(a^{-1})$, hence $T_{as}=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(a)T_s$ for $a\in P$, which gives the same extension formula. Changing the geometric base point gives the change-of-base-point isomorphism, using the paths of [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport]. Every later expression $\rho:W(X_0)\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ refers to this extension, not merely to the geometric representation.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, let $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, assume that $X$ is
connected, and choose a geometric point $\bar x\to X$. Let
$\mathcal F_0$ be a lisse
Weil sheaf, with underlying lisse
$\Qlb$-sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ in the convention of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Put
$V=\mathcal F_{\bar x}$. The underlying lisse sheaf first gives the
*geometric fundamental representation*

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}:\pi_1(X,\bar x)\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)
$$

by the equivalence of
*lisse $\Qlb$-sheaves on a connected scheme with continuous
$\Qlb$-representations of its etale fundamental group* of
[cor-galois-lisse-representations], the fundamental group being the
automorphism group of the fibre functor as in
[def-galois-fibre-functor]
($k$-torsion and adic levels are as in the coefficient conventions of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]).

The Weil descent datum
$\varphi:\Phi_X^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$, with
$\Phi_X$ as in [def-tw-frobenius-action], supplies the missing
degree-one operator. More explicitly, let

$$
W(X_0,\bar x):=
\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)\times_{\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)}
\langle\Phi_X\rangle
$$

be the inverse image of the infinite cyclic subgroup generated by
geometric Frobenius, and choose a lift $s$ of $\Phi_X$. After the
usual transport of the stalk from $\Phi_X(\bar x)$ to $\bar x$, the
datum $\varphi$ gives an automorphism $T_s$ of $V$ satisfying

$$
T_s\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(\gamma)T_s^{-1}
=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(s\gamma s^{-1})
\qquad(\gamma\in\pi_1(X,\bar x)).
$$

The *Weil fundamental representation* of $\mathcal F_0$ is the
extension of $\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}$ to $W(X_0,\bar x)$ defined by

$$
\rho(\gamma s^n):=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(\gamma)T_s^n
\qquad(\gamma\in\pi_1(X,\bar x),\ n\in\mathbf Z).
$$

Every later expression $\rho:W(X_0)\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ refers to
this extension, not merely to the geometric representation.

This formula defines a continuous representation, and the resulting
representation depends on the auxiliary choices only up to the
change-of-base-point isomorphism.

The new correspondence is independent of this definition and of all Weil-group nodes, preventing the cycle through the existing finite-etale Weil-transport theorem. Correct transport-node metadata and missing notion citations. No Lean or compilation.

lean.note: Section 1(B): the upstream fundamentalRep accepts an arbitrary WeilMonodromyData, whose geomEquiv is not tied to the arithmetic inclusion determined by BasePointData.path. This is unusable for evaluating the specified geometric inertia subgroups. The module retains upstream fundamentalRep and fixes its geometric identification and Frobenius lift uniquely by their images under W.toFundamentalGroup: B.geomAut and B.frobAut. It then specializes fundamentalRep to these canonical data. No arbitrary equivalence or arbitrary map is chosen.
